candidates.label: Three Taverns (Tres Tabernae, Appian Way)
candidates.support: A station on the Appian Way about 33 Roman miles from Rome. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site.

summary.text: Three Taverns was a station on the Appian Way about thirty-three Roman miles from Rome, where a road from Antium to Norba crossed the main highway. According to Acts, as Paul, under guard as a prisoner, approached Rome, one group of believers from the city went as far as Forum of Appius, a station farther from Rome, while another awaited him at Three Taverns.

history.text: About 10 km south toward Forum of Appius lay Tripontium, which the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia names as the point where the Appian Way entered the region of the Pontine Marshes.

scripture.textWEB: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
